trip.title: Bier Reisen 2020
trip.subtitle: The trip that started it: Munich, Bamberg, Düsseldorf, the Trappists and back

stops.name: Porto Alegre
stops.note: Departure, 2 February — overnight flight to Munich.

stops.name: Munich (arrival)
stops.note: Hotel Royal. First night, first Maß.

stops.name: Bamberg
stops.note: Ibis Styles. Rauchbier country in the UNESCO old town.

stops.name: Düsseldorf
stops.note: Altstadt Hotel Rheinblick, two nights in the Altstadt.

stops.name: La Trappe
stops.note: Brouwerij La Trappe — the only Trappist brewery in the Netherlands, on the way south.

stops.name: Antwerp
stops.note: Hotel Banks. Kulminator and the cathedral quarter.

stops.name: Brussels
stops.note: Ibis Brussels City Centre. Cantillon, Moeder Lambic, the Grand Place.

stops.name: Ghent (lunch)
stops.note: Lunch stop on the way to Bruges — Gruut and the Graslei.

stops.name: Bruges
stops.note: Martin's Brugge. De Halve Maan, De Garre, the Markt at night.

stops.name: Westvleteren
stops.note: Sint-Sixtus Abbey and In de Vrede — the reason this road exists.

stops.name: Chimay (Poteaupré)
stops.note: Auberge de Poteaupré, the abbey's own inn, at the edge of the forest.

stops.name: Zwiefaltendorf
stops.note: Bauer am Bach and dinner at Blank's Brauerei — a Swabian village brewery on the Danube.

stops.name: Munich (return)
stops.note: Hotel Royal again, four nights: the long Munich finish.

stops.name: Munich Airport
stops.note: 17 February — fly home, land in Porto Alegre on the 18th.

days.title: Porto Alegre → Munich
items: Overnight flight POA → MUC (10,698 km, ~13 h 35 in the air)
Dinner at the airport before boarding
Sleep on the plane — Munich starts the next morning

days.title: Arrive Munich
items: Land at Franz Josef Strauss, train into town
Hotel Royal, first walk through the Altstadt
Evening: Augustiner or Schneider, whichever is closer to the hotel

days.title: Munich → Bamberg
items: 232 km / 2 h 31 north on the A9 and A70
Ibis Styles, then the old town on foot
Evening at Schlenkerla: Rauchbier from the oak barrel

days.title: Bamberg → Düsseldorf
items: 425 km / 4 h 25 west across Franconia and the Rhineland
Altstadt Hotel Rheinblick, check in
First Altbier at Uerige, straight from the barrel

days.title: Düsseldorf
items: Altbier crawl in the Altstadt: Uerige, Schumacher, Füchschen, Schlüssel
Rheinturm and the MedienHafen if the weather holds
Dinner with Altbier, not wine — the local rule

days.title: Düsseldorf → La Trappe → Antwerp
items: 141 km / 1 h 45 to Berkel-Enschot
Brouwerij La Trappe tour and tasting — the Dutch Trappist
81 km / 1 h 03 to Antwerp; Hotel Banks, then Kulminator

days.title: Antwerp → Brussels
items: 47 km / 0 h 49 south
Ibis Brussels City Centre, drop the bags
Cantillon in the afternoon, Moeder Lambic in the evening

days.title: Brussels
items: Cantillon brewery tour — lambic, gueuze, kriek
A la Mort Subite for the 1928 room
Grand Place at night, then Delirium or Poechenellekelder

days.title: Brussels → Ghent → Bruges
items: 59 km / 0 h 56 to Ghent for lunch
Gruut city brewery and the Graslei
47 km / 0 h 41 on to Bruges; Martin's Brugge, De Garre at night

days.title: Bruges → Westvleteren → Chimay
items: 72 km / 1 h 06 to Sint-Sixtus; In de Vrede for Westvleteren 12
189 km / 2 h 32 south-east through the Walloon countryside
Auberge de Poteaupré — Chimay at the source, dinner included

days.title: Chimay → Zwiefaltendorf
items: 573 km / 6 h 54 — the long transfer day
Bauer am Bach in Zwiefaltendorf, on the Danube
Dinner at Blank's Brauerei: Swabian village beer

days.title: Zwiefaltendorf → Munich
items: 186 km / 2 h 12 south-east on the B311 and A96
Hotel Royal for the last four nights
Evening at Augustiner-Keller

days.title: Munich
items: Schneider Bräuhaus for Aventinus
Hofbräuhaus once, for the room
Viktualienmarkt and the beer garden if it is open

days.title: Munich
items: Giesinger Bräu in the south of the city
Deutsches Museum or the Pinakothek in the afternoon
Dinner at a Brauhaus, Maß in hand

days.title: Munich
items: Day trip to Andechs if the weather is clear (Kloster Andechs, Doppelbock)
Or Freising for Weihenstephan
Last night in the Altstadt

days.title: Munich → Airport
items: 39 km / 0 h 35 to Franz Josef Strauss
Return the car, check in
Overnight flight home

days.title: Home
items: Land in Porto Alegre on 18 February
17 days, 14 nights, 5 breweries and one Trappist abbey at dawn

Munich (arrival).name: Augustiner-Keller
Munich (arrival).note: Munich's oldest brewery and the locals' choice; Edelstoff from wooden barrels under the chestnuts.
Munich (arrival).order: Edelstoff by the Maß, and stay for the second

Munich (arrival).name: Schneider Bräuhaus
Munich (arrival).note: The original wheat-beer house; Aventinus is the benchmark Weizenbock.
Munich (arrival).order: Aventinus, then the Eisbock if it is listed

Munich (arrival).name: Hofbräuhaus
Munich (arrival).note: Brewing since 1589 — go once for the room.
Munich (arrival).order: Hofbräu Original in the main hall, with the brass band

Munich (arrival).name: Giesinger Bräu
Munich (arrival).note: Garage-to-glory craft brewery in the south; Erhellung unfiltered Helles.

Bamberg.name: Schlenkerla
Bamberg.note: Rauchbier since 1405, beechwood-smoked malt from oak barrels in a medieval vaulted cellar.
Bamberg.order: Aecht Schlenkerla Rauchbier Märzen, beechwood smoke from the oak barrel

Bamberg.name: Spezial
Bamberg.note: The locals' rauchbier — subtler smoke than Schlenkerla.
Bamberg.order: Spezial Rauchbier Lager — the locals' answer to Schlenkerla

Bamberg.name: Mahr's Bräu
Bamberg.note: The legendary 'aU' Ungespundetes, naturally carbonated and unfiltered.
Bamberg.order: aU Ungespundetes, the reference Franconian lager

Bamberg.name: Fässla
Bamberg.note: Zwergla dark lager, brewery tap opposite Spezial.

Bamberg.name: Greifenklau
Bamberg.note: Beer garden with the best view over the city.
Bamberg.order: Lagerbier on the terrace — the walk up is the point

Düsseldorf.name: Uerige
Düsseldorf.note: The reference Altbier: copper kettles, waiters who never stop pouring, and a house bitter enough to reset your palate.
Düsseldorf.order: Uerige Alt — bitter, copper-brewed, and the waiter never stops pouring

Düsseldorf.name: Brauerei Schumacher
Düsseldorf.note: Oldest Altbier brewery in the city, blond and spritzy, in a tiled 19th-century hall.
Düsseldorf.order: Schumacher Alt, then the Jubiläums-Alt if it is on

Düsseldorf.name: Im Füchschen
Düsseldorf.note: Altbier and Rhineland food in the Altstadt's busiest corner.
Düsseldorf.order: Füchschen Alt with a plate of Rheinischer Sauerbraten

Düsseldorf.name: Zum Schlüssel
Düsseldorf.note: Brewpub with a copper kettle in the cellar and a quieter room upstairs.
Düsseldorf.order: Schlüssel Alt, from the copper kettle in the cellar

La Trappe.name: Brouwerij La Trappe
La Trappe.note: The only Dutch Trappist brewery, at Berkel-Enschot near Tilburg: Witte, Blond, Dubbel, Tripel and the barrel-aged Quadrupel.
La Trappe.order: Quadrupel, and the barrel-aged version if the shop still has it

Antwerp.name: Kulminator
Antwerp.note: 700+ bottles with vintages going back decades; the cellar list is the reason to come.
Antwerp.order: A vintage gueuze or an old Duvel from the cellar list

Antwerp.name: Billie's Bier Kafétaria
Antwerp.note: 300+ beers in a cosy neighbourhood room, staff who know the list.
Antwerp.order: Whatever the staff recommend from the 300 — tell them what you liked last

Antwerp.name: De Koninck City Brewery
Antwerp.note: The Antwerp classic, Bolleke in its bowl-shaped glass.
Antwerp.order: Bolleke, then the brewery tour through the koelschip

Brussels.name: Cantillon
Brussels.note: The last traditional lambic brewery inside the city: coolship, barrels, Gueuze and Kriek with no sweetening.
Brussels.order: Gueuze 100% Lambic Bio, then the Kriek at the barrel room

Brussels.name: Moeder Lambic
Brussels.note: 40 taps of rare Belgian craft; the best introduction to the modern scene.
Brussels.order: Something sour on tap — ask what is open from the wood

Brussels.name: A la Mort Subite
Brussels.note: 1928 Art Deco café; order the house gueuze at the bar.
Brussels.order: House gueuze at the bar of the 1928 room

Brussels.name: Poechenellekelder
Brussels.note: Puppet-themed pub opposite Manneken Pis, 100+ Belgian beers.
Brussels.order: A Trappist or a Flemish red, opposite Manneken Pis

Ghent.name: Gruut Stadsbrouwerij
Ghent.note: City brewery using a medieval herb-and-spice mix instead of hops.
Ghent.order: Gruut Wit or Blond — the medieval herb mix is the house signature

Ghent.name: De Dulle Griet
Ghent.note: 500 beers on the Vrijdagmarkt, and the shoe-in-the-basket ritual.
Ghent.order: Anything from the 500-bottle list, with your shoe in the basket

Ghent.name: Het Waterhuis aan de Bierkant
Ghent.order: A Flemish red on the canal

Bruges.name: De Halve Maan
Bruges.note: Only active brewery in the historic centre; Brugse Zot and Straffe Hendrik, with the 3 km beer pipeline.
Bruges.order: Brugse Zot blond, then Straffe Hendrik Quadrupel

Bruges.name: De Garre
Bruges.note: Hidden alley café, house tripel at 11%, maximum three per person.
Bruges.order: The house Tripel with the cube of cheese — and stop at three

Bruges.name: 't Brugs Beertje
Bruges.note: 300+ bottles, the classic brown bar of Bruges.
Bruges.order: A vintage Flemish red from the 300+ list

Bruges.name: Café Vlissinghe
Bruges.note: Oldest pub in Bruges (1515), bocce court in the garden.
Bruges.order: A West Flanders blonde in the 1515 room, then bocce in the garden

Westvleteren.name: In de Vrede
Westvleteren.note: The café opposite Sint-Sixtus: the only reliable place to drink Westvleteren 12 on tap, with the abbey cheese.
Westvleteren.order: Westvleteren 12 by the glass — the 8 if you are driving — and the abbey cheese

Westvleteren.name: Sint-Sixtus Abbey
Westvleteren.note: The Trappist monastery itself — no tours, but the gate and the shop are part of the pilgrimage.
Westvleteren.order: Whatever the gate shop allows — six bottles per person, booked ahead

Chimay (Poteaupré).name: Auberge de Poteaupré
Chimay (Poteaupré).note: The abbey's own inn and restaurant, a few hundred metres from Scourmont; Chimay Blue with abbey cheese.
Chimay (Poteaupré).order: Chimay Bleue with the Scourmont cheese board

Chimay (Poteaupré).name: Chimay Scourmont Abbey
Chimay (Poteaupré).note: The largest Trappist brewery; the Espace Chimay explains the brewing and the cheese.
Chimay (Poteaupré).order: The Espace Chimay flight — Rouge, Blanche, Bleue side by side

Zwiefaltendorf.name: Blank's Brauerei
Zwiefaltendorf.note: Village brewery and Gasthof on the Danube — Swabian Landbier, roast pork and no pretence.
Zwiefaltendorf.order: Blank's Landbier and a Schnitzel; the drive is tomorrow

Munich (return).name: Augustiner-Keller
Munich (return).note: Wooden-barrel Edelstoff under the chestnuts; the locals' answer to every tourist beer hall.
Munich (return).order: Edelstoff, again, because it is the best thing in the city

Munich (return).name: Schneider Bräuhaus
Munich (return).note: Wheat-beer masters, Aventinus and the original Tap7.
Munich (return).order: Aventinus Eisbock if it is on

Munich (return).name: Hofbräuhaus
Munich (return).note: The room everyone has heard of; go early or late.
Munich (return).order: Dunkel this time, in the upstairs room

Munich (return).name: Giesinger Bräu
Munich (return).note: Munich craft with a neighbourhood taproom.

Munich (return).name: Kloster Andechs (day trip)
Munich (return).note: Benedictine monastery brewery above the Ammersee — Doppelbock Dunkel, 45 km from the city.
Munich (return).order: Doppelbock Dunkel on the terrace above the Ammersee

Munich (arrival).subnote: Hotel Royal, the first night, and the Altstadt on foot.

Bamberg.subnote: Ibis Styles, the UNESCO old town, and five breweries within walking distance.

Düsseldorf.subnote: Altstadt Hotel Rheinblick, in the middle of the Altstadt's Altbier mile.
Düsseldorf.famous: Altbier, poured straight from the barrel

La Trappe.subnote: The only Dutch Trappist brewery, at Berkel-Enschot near Tilburg.
La Trappe.famous: Trappist ale — Witte, Dubbel, Tripel, Quadrupel

Antwerp.subnote: Hotel Banks, the cathedral quarter, and the deepest beer cellar in Belgium.

Brussels.subnote: Ibis Brussels City Centre; Cantillon on one side, the Grand Place on the other.

Ghent.subnote: An afternoon between Brussels and Bruges: herb beer and the Graslei.
Ghent.famous: Gruut — beer brewed with herbs instead of hops

Bruges.subnote: Martin's Brugge, the Markt at night, and De Garre down an alley.
Bruges.famous: Brugse Zot and the 11% house tripel

Westvleteren.subnote: Sint-Sixtus Abbey and In de Vrede — the reason this road exists.

Chimay (Poteaupré).subnote: Auberge de Poteaupré, the abbey's own inn at the edge of the forest.
Chimay (Poteaupré).famous: Chimay Blue and the abbey cheese

Zwiefaltendorf.subnote: Bauer am Bach on the Danube, dinner at a village brewery.

Munich (return).subnote: Hotel Royal again for the long finish, with Andechs as a day trip.
Munich (return).famous: The full Munich range, one last time
